capsuleTopic.title: Creation
capsuleTopic.subtitle: God · ordered world · humanity · image · garden · rest · rupture · memory · new creation
capsuleTopic.orientation: Do not turn Creation into a list of doctrines or a debate on arrival. First watch the event itself: who acts, what is spoken, what is separated, named, blessed, formed, placed, commanded, completed, and later remembered. Let Genesis 1–2 remain distinct literary movements while later Scripture reopens their language from different vantage points.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Enter Creation as an event with a primary actor and human focal characters. Move from the broad ordering of the world to the close-up of humanity and Eden, then watch immediate rupture and later biblical memory without letting later passages erase the wording or genre of Genesis.

passages.title: Before the first command
passages.excerpt: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.  The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
passages.observation: Before light, land, creatures, or humanity appear, the scene already contains God, heavens and earth, darkness, the deep, waters, and Spirit.
